1.title: Dictatorship, Aggression, Neutrality, and the Road to World War II
vocab: totalitarianism
A political system in which the state seeks broad control over public and private life.
appeasement
A policy of granting concessions to an aggressor in hopes of avoiding a larger conflict.
Neutrality Acts
United States laws intended to limit American involvement in foreign wars during the 1930s.
cash-and-carry
A policy allowing belligerents to buy certain goods if they paid immediately and transported them themselves.
Lend-Lease Act
A 1941 law authorizing the United States to provide war supplies to nations considered vital to American defense.
facts: Which event began the European war in September 1939?
Germany's invasion of Poland
Japan's attack on Pearl Harbor
Italy's invasion of Ethiopia
The Munich Agreement
Why did the Neutrality Acts reflect isolationist sentiment?
They attempted to keep Americans and American trade from drawing the nation into foreign wars.
They required the United States to join every European alliance.
They immediately declared war on Germany.
They transferred control of foreign policy to Britain.
Which statement best explains the shift from neutrality to Lend-Lease?
The United States increasingly aided nations resisting Axis aggression while remaining formally outside the war.
The United States ended all trade with Britain.
Congress surrendered its war powers to Germany.
The United States joined the Axis alliance.
What did the Munich Agreement reveal about appeasement?
Concessions did not prevent Hitler from pursuing further expansion.
It permanently ended German territorial demands.
It caused the United States to declare war in 1938.
It created the United Nations.
Why is the Atlantic Charter historically significant?
It expressed shared Anglo-American principles for the postwar world before formal U.S. entry.
It was the formal surrender of Japan.
It divided Germany into occupation zones.
It authorized Japanese American incarceration.

2.title: Pearl Harbor, Mobilization, and America's Entry into World War II
vocab: Pearl Harbor
The U.S. naval base attacked by Japan on December 7, 1941, prompting American entry into World War II.
embargo
A government restriction or prohibition on trade with another country.
mobilization
The organization of a nation's people, industry, and resources for war.
Selective Training and Service Act
The 1940 law that established the first peacetime military draft in U.S. history.
War Production Board
The federal agency that directed conversion of civilian industry to military production.
facts: What was the immediate U.S. response to the attack on Pearl Harbor?
Congress declared war on Japan after President Roosevelt requested it.
Congress declared neutrality permanent.
The United States withdrew from the Pacific.
The United States joined the Axis.
How did the U.S. oil embargo affect relations with Japan?
It increased pressure on Japan by limiting access to a resource essential for military expansion.
It guaranteed a diplomatic settlement.
It supplied Japan with additional fuel.
It ended Japanese expansion in China immediately.
Which sequence is chronologically correct?
Japanese expansion, U.S. economic pressure, failed negotiations, Pearl Harbor, U.S. declaration of war
Pearl Harbor, Neutrality Acts, invasion of Poland, oil embargo, Lend-Lease
U.S. declaration of war, Pearl Harbor, oil embargo, failed negotiations
War Production Board, Munich Agreement, Pearl Harbor, invasion of Poland
What was a central purpose of the War Production Board?
To coordinate production priorities and shift industry toward military needs
To command combat operations in Europe
To negotiate peace with Japan
To decide Supreme Court cases
Why is Pearl Harbor considered a turning point?
It transformed the United States from an armed supporter of the Allies into a formal combatant.
It ended World War II immediately.
It began the Great Depression.
It caused Germany to surrender before the United States entered the war.

3.title: Fighting World War II: Europe, the Pacific, and Global Strategy
vocab: Europe First
The Allied strategy of prioritizing the defeat of Nazi Germany while containing Japan.
island hopping
The Pacific strategy of capturing selected islands while bypassing heavily fortified positions.
D-Day
The Allied invasion of Normandy on June 6, 1944.
Battle of Midway
The 1942 naval battle that weakened Japanese carrier strength and shifted momentum in the Pacific.
V-E Day
May 8, 1945, marking the end of the war in Europe.
facts: Why did the Allies adopt the Europe First strategy?
They viewed Nazi Germany as the most immediate strategic threat while still resisting Japan.
They had already defeated Germany before Pearl Harbor.
They planned to abandon the Pacific permanently.
They believed Japan was allied with Britain.
What made the Battle of Midway a major turning point?
American forces destroyed key Japanese carriers and shifted the strategic initiative.
It opened the Normandy beachhead.
It caused Germany's surrender.
It was fought entirely in North Africa.
What was the strategic purpose of D-Day?
To establish an Allied foothold in Western Europe and open a major front against Germany
To capture Tokyo
To defend Pearl Harbor from its first attack
To end the Battle of the Atlantic in 1941
How did island hopping support the Allied advance?
It secured useful bases and moved forces toward Japan while bypassing some strongholds.
It required capturing every Japanese-held island.
It shifted all forces away from the Pacific.
It was a diplomatic agreement with the Soviet Union.
Which evidence best supports the claim that World War II required global strategy?
Allied leaders coordinated campaigns, shipping, resources, and priorities across Europe, Africa, Asia, and the Pacific.
Every battle occurred in one country.
Civilian production was unrelated to military operations.
The Allies fought without coordinating objectives.

4.title: The American Home Front: Mobilization, Race, Women, and Civil Liberties
vocab: rationing
Government limits on civilian purchases of scarce goods so resources could support the war effort.
Double V campaign
The campaign for victory over fascism abroad and racism at home.
Executive Order 9066
The 1942 order used to authorize military exclusion zones and the forced removal of Japanese Americans.
Rosie the Riveter
A wartime symbol encouraging women to enter industrial employment.
Bracero Program
A wartime agreement that brought Mexican laborers to work temporarily in the United States.
facts: What contradiction did the Double V campaign emphasize?
The nation fought dictatorship abroad while African Americans continued to face racism at home.
The United States fought on only one military front.
Factories produced no civilian goods.
Women were prohibited from wartime work.
What did Executive Order 8802 address?
Discrimination in defense industries and federal employment
The invasion of Normandy
The creation of the United Nations
The surrender of Japan
Why is Japanese American incarceration a major civil-liberties issue?
People were forcibly removed and confined largely on the basis of ancestry without individualized proof of disloyalty.
It expanded due-process protections for every resident.
It applied only to convicted enemy soldiers.
It was ordered after individual criminal trials.
How did wartime labor demands affect women?
They opened many industrial and military-support roles, although inequality and pressure to leave work persisted.
They permanently ended all workplace discrimination.
They barred women from paid employment.
They eliminated childcare needs.
Which comparison best captures the home-front experience?
Mobilization expanded opportunity and production while also exposing persistent inequality and rights violations.
Every group experienced identical benefits.
The war produced only restrictions and no opportunities.
Military victory automatically ended discrimination.

5.title: The Holocaust, Refugees, and the American Response
vocab: Holocaust
The systematic persecution and murder of six million Jews and millions of other victims by Nazi Germany and its collaborators.
antisemitism
Prejudice, hostility, or discrimination directed against Jewish people.
Final Solution
The Nazi plan for the systematic murder of Europe's Jews.
War Refugee Board
The U.S. agency created in 1944 to aid and rescue victims of Nazi persecution.
genocide
Acts committed with intent to destroy, in whole or in part, a national, ethnic, racial, or religious group.
facts: What was the purpose of the Nuremberg Laws?
To strip Jews of citizenship and legal rights and institutionalize racial persecution
To protect refugees entering the United States
To establish the United Nations
To prosecute Nazi leaders after the war
Why is the term Final Solution historically important?
It referred to the Nazi plan to systematically murder Europe's Jews.
It described the Allied invasion of France.
It was the American plan for rebuilding Japan.
It ended antisemitic laws in Germany.
Which factor limited the American response to Jewish refugees before and during much of the war?
Restrictive immigration quotas, administrative barriers, prejudice, and political caution
A complete lack of information about persecution
A constitutional ban on all immigration
German control of all American ports
What did the War Refugee Board represent?
A late but important federal effort to rescue and assist people threatened by Nazi persecution
The agency that designed concentration camps
The Allied military command for D-Day
The court that decided Korematsu
Why must Holocaust evidence be corroborated across different source types?
Victim testimony, perpetrator records, photographs, artifacts, and demographic evidence together establish context and counter distortion.
One anonymous claim is always sufficient.
Only government documents can reveal human experience.
Corroboration eliminates the need to examine source purpose.

6.title: Atomic Bombs, Victory, and the Postwar Settlement
vocab: Manhattan Project
The secret Allied program that developed the atomic bomb during World War II.
Hiroshima
The Japanese city on which the United States dropped the first atomic bomb used in war on August 6, 1945.
Nagasaki
The Japanese city on which the United States dropped a second atomic bomb on August 9, 1945.
Yalta Conference
The February 1945 meeting at which Allied leaders discussed the final war effort and postwar arrangements.
United Nations
The international organization established in 1945 to promote cooperation and collective security.
topics: Soviet entry into war against Japan
facts: What was the Manhattan Project?
A secret program to research and build an atomic weapon
The Allied invasion of Italy
A plan for Japanese American removal
An economic aid program for Europe
Which statement best represents responsible analysis of the atomic-bomb decision?
It weighs military estimates, alternatives, Soviet entry, Japanese decision-making, civilian harm, and uncertainty in the evidence.
It assumes one motive explains every decision.
It ignores civilian consequences.
It treats later outcomes as fully predictable in 1945.
How were Yalta and Potsdam connected?
Both addressed the defeat of the Axis and postwar order, but Potsdam occurred after Germany's surrender and amid growing Allied tension.
Both occurred before the United States entered the war.
Both created the Axis alliance.
Both were meetings between only Japan and Germany.
What was one major purpose of the United Nations?
To provide a continuing forum for international cooperation and collective security
To replace every national government
To divide the United States into occupation zones
To administer the Neutrality Acts
Why did victory in 1945 not produce a simple return to prewar conditions?
The war altered global power, created occupation responsibilities, exposed mass destruction, and produced new international institutions and tensions.
The United States immediately withdrew from all world affairs.
European empires became stronger everywhere.
Atomic weapons had no diplomatic significance.

7.title: Containment, Truman Doctrine, Marshall Plan, Berlin, and Korea
vocab: containment
The strategy of limiting the expansion of Soviet influence rather than attempting immediate rollback everywhere.
Truman Doctrine
The 1947 policy pledging U.S. support to peoples resisting coercion, initially focused on Greece and Turkey.
Marshall Plan
The American program of economic aid designed to support European recovery and political stability.
Berlin Airlift
The 1948–1949 Allied operation that supplied West Berlin during the Soviet blockade.
NATO
The collective-defense alliance formed in 1949 by the United States, Canada, and Western European nations.
facts: What was the central goal of containment?
To prevent further expansion of Soviet influence
To restore Axis governments
To end all American alliances
To annex Western Europe
How did the Marshall Plan support containment?
Economic recovery was intended to strengthen European stability and reduce the appeal of communism.
It supplied atomic weapons to every European country.
It ended all trade with Europe.
It required Western Europe to join the Soviet bloc.
What did the Berlin Airlift demonstrate?
The Western Allies could resist pressure and sustain West Berlin without directly attacking Soviet forces.
The Allies abandoned West Berlin.
Germany was reunified in 1948.
NATO dissolved before it was created.
Why was NATO historically significant?
It committed member states to collective defense and marked a lasting U.S. security role in Europe.
It was a temporary wartime rationing agency.
It transferred Western Europe to Soviet control.
It ended the Korean War before it began.
How did the Korean War test containment?
The United States and United Nations intervened after North Korea invaded South Korea, seeking to resist expansion without starting a wider world war.
It was fought to restore Japanese rule in Korea.
It caused the immediate dissolution of the Soviet Union.
It involved no international forces.
